about: The code examples of the chapter 13 deck, in the order of the code slides (order = slide order). The page's chapter-code tab lists them by NAME in this order; every example is self-contained and runs with the Python standard library only, opens no network connection, reads no keyboard and opens no window (a page in a browser cannot reach the web, so the third-party tools of the chapter are shown by their standard-library counterparts and by small stand-ins, named beside the code); the expected result is what the run printed in a fresh interpreter. The code is exactly the text of the deck's code boxes with the '>>> ' prompt removed.

page_requirements: The Python standard library modules urllib.parse, urllib.request (urlopen on a data: address), urllib.robotparser, http, webbrowser (the examples replace webbrowser.open by a recording function), json, os, tempfile, re, contextlib, html.parser and xml.etree.ElementTree (imported by the examples that use them), and the built-ins print, repr, len, range, enumerate, round, type, list, dict
A writable temporary folder (the chunks example); no subprocess, no keyboard input, no network, no browser window

examples.name: A URL cut into its parts
examples.code:
from urllib.parse import urlsplit
url = ('https://api.openweathermap.org/geo/1.0/direct'
       '?q=Boston&appid=KEY#top')
parts = urlsplit(url)
for name in ('scheme', 'netloc', 'path', 'query', 'fragment'):
    print(name.ljust(8), getattr(parts, name))
examples.expected:
scheme   https
netloc   api.openweathermap.org
path     /geo/1.0/direct
query    q=Boston&appid=KEY
fragment top

examples.name: HTTP status codes and their classes
examples.code:
from http import HTTPStatus
for code in (200, 301, 404, 429, 500):
    status = HTTPStatus(code)
    print(code, status.phrase, '| class', code // 100)
examples.expected:
200 OK | class 2
301 Moved Permanently | class 3
404 Not Found | class 4
429 Too Many Requests | class 4
500 Internal Server Error | class 5

examples.name: robots.txt rules with can_fetch
examples.code:
import urllib.robotparser as rp
robots = rp.RobotFileParser()
robots.parse(['User-agent: *', 'Disallow: /simple/',
              'Disallow: /account/'])
for path in ('/project/x/', '/simple/x/', '/account/login/'):
    print(path, robots.can_fetch('*', 'https://pypi.org' + path))

examples.name: Crawl-delay and a polite pause
examples.code:
import urllib.robotparser as rp
robots = rp.RobotFileParser()
robots.parse(['User-agent: *', 'Crawl-delay: 2',
              'Request-rate: 3/20'])
pause = robots.crawl_delay('*')
rate = robots.request_rate('*')
print('wait', pause, 'seconds; rate', tuple(rate))
for page, clock in zip('abc', range(0, 6, pause)):
    print('t =', clock, 'fetch page', page)
examples.expected:
wait 2 seconds; rate (3, 20)
t = 0 fetch page a
t = 2 fetch page b
t = 4 fetch page c

examples.name: Resolve, defragment and de-duplicate links
examples.code:
from urllib.parse import urljoin, urldefrag
site = 'https://example.com'
page = site + '/guide/index.html'
hrefs = ['intro.html', 'intro.html#top', '/about',
         'https://other.org/x']
seen = []
for href in hrefs:
    full, fragment = urldefrag(urljoin(page, href))
    if full.startswith(site) and full not in seen:
        seen.append(full)
print(seen)
